record.title: OpenAI reports large gains on coding evaluations for low-resource programming languages
record.summary: In an Oct 19 post, OpenAI reports improved results for GPT-6 models on two coding evaluations involving lower-resource languages. On MultiLangBench, which asks models to build a SQLite-compatible database engine across 20 languages, OpenAI reports an average test pass rate of 87.4% for GPT-6 Astra versus 26.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol; GPT-6 Luna scores 40.3% at a stated approximately 78% lower estimated API cost. On a separate COBOL migration evaluation, OpenAI reports 86.6% accuracy for GPT-6.1 Sol at low reasoning effort versus 5.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol, and 97.9% at higher effort. OpenAI released the MultiLangBench setup and test suite. These are company-reported evaluation results, not independently reproduced or evidence of production migration safety.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI reports that GPT-6 Astra achieved an average 87.4% test pass rate on MultiLangBench across 20 languages versus 26.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol; GPT-6 Luna scored 40.3% at approximately 78% lower estimated API cost than GPT-5.6 Sol.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI reports 86.6% accuracy for GPT-6.1 Sol at low reasoning effort on its COBOL migration evaluation versus 5.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol at the same setting, with GPT-6.1 Sol reaching 97.9% at higher effort.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The public OpenAI MultiLangBench repository describes a SQLite 3.40.1 implementation task and test construction from SQLite TCL tests; it states 24,000 of 51,000 source tests were converted and recommends a 272-test subset for ordinary lower-cost comparisons.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reported scores do not establish independently reproduced performance, behavior preservation in production systems, reduced expert-review burden, or realized economic savings.

evidence_gaps.description: Neither evaluation's reported scores have been independently reproduced; repeated-run uncertainty and exact model prompts/settings were not inspected.

The repository README notes 24,000 convertible tests from 51,000 SQLite TCL tests and recommends a 272-test subset for ordinary comparisons; how the reported averages vary across sampled tests and language-specific coverage is not established here.
The COBOL migration evaluation details and a public runnable artifact were not located in the inspected post and linked repository.
No production migrations, behavior drift rates, expert-review costs, deployment outcomes or economic savings were measured in the inspected sources.

OpenAI says per-language results accompany the released evaluation, but the inspected repository root exposes no separate result table/file and the inspected README sections do not show per-language scores; the result artifact path remains unidentified.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported gains generalize, better coding and behavior-preserving migration in languages such as COBOL and Fortran could reduce a meaningful software-maintenance bottleneck for organizations with legacy systems. Current evidence is first-party controlled-evaluation reporting; external reproduction and production impact are unestablished.
limitations: The performance figures are OpenAI-reported; the research desk did not execute or reproduce either evaluation.
The public repository documents MultiLangBench, but the described SQLite task is not a direct measure of general software maintenance or full production migration.

The repository README says 24,000 of 51,000 SQLite TCL tests were converted and recommends a 272-test subset for routine lower-cost evaluations; representativeness of that subset remains to be assessed.
The inspected public repository does not document the separate COBOL migration evaluation's task corpus or hidden-test design.
The post itself says production migration requires expert review and testing against system business rules and dependencies; production safety and realized economic impact are not established.

The inspected GitHub repository root exposes the README, requirements, scripts and tests but no separate per-language result file; the OpenAI post says such results are released, and their artifact location was not identified in this pass.
brief.summary: In an Oct 19 post, OpenAI reports improved results for GPT-6 models on two coding evaluations involving lower-resource languages. On MultiLangBench, which asks models to build a SQLite-compatible database engine across 20 languages, OpenAI reports an average test pass rate of 87.4% for GPT-6 Astra versus 26.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol; GPT-6 Luna scores 40.3% at a stated approximately 78% lower estimated API cost. On a separate COBOL migration evaluation, OpenAI reports 86.6% accuracy for GPT-6.1 Sol at low reasoning effort versus 5.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol, and 97.9% at higher effort. technical.claimed_result: OpenAI reports GPT-6 Astra at 87.4% average test pass rate across 20 MultiLangBench languages versus GPT-5.6 Sol at 26.8%; GPT-6 Luna at 40.3% and approximately 78% lower estimated API cost than GPT-5.6 Sol; and GPT-6.1 Sol at 86.6% low-effort / 97.9% higher-effort accuracy on its COBOL migration evaluation versus GPT-5.6 Sol at 5.4% low effort.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary sources demonstrate that OpenAI published these reported comparisons and released the MultiLangBench setup and test suite. The underlying comparative performance has not been independently reproduced by the research desk.
technical.mechanism: MultiLangBench asks a model to build a SQLite-compatible database engine in a selected language and checks database outputs against reference SQLite queries. The separate migration evaluation asks models to translate COBOL programs to C++, Java, Kotlin, Python or Rust while preserving observable outputs under hidden tests, as described by OpenAI.
technical.regime: MultiLangBench: 20 programming languages, SQLite-compatible implementation, reported maximum reasoning effort for the cited Astra/Luna aggregate scores. COBOL migration: OpenAI reports low and higher reasoning effort, but the inspected page does not provide full task-set or repeated-run details. All scores are first-party claims.
technical.strongest_baseline: OpenAI compares GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Luna with GPT-5.6 Sol on MultiLangBench, and GPT-6.1 Sol with GPT-5.6 Sol at the same low reasoning setting on COBOL migration. The inspected source does not establish cross-lab comparability or independent replication.

brief.title: OpenAI reports large gains on coding evaluations for low-resource programming languages
brief.why_it_matters: COBOL, Fortran and other languages with smaller training and documentation corpora remain embedded in important software. Stronger coding and behavior-preserving migration could reduce a practical maintenance bottleneck if these results transfer to real repositories. The evidence currently measures controlled evaluation tasks, and expert review and system-specific testing remain necessary; neither production impact nor economic savings are established.
